paragraphs: Probabilistic neurosymbolic learning combines neural networks with reasoning expressed through logical rules and probabilities. Exact reasoning in existing frameworks can require computation that grows exponentially with the problem, restricting the size of tasks they can handle. A-NeSI addresses this bottleneck by learning neural networks that approximate the inference process.

The framework performs approximate inference in polynomial time while retaining the meaning of the underlying probabilistic logic. It trains on examples generated from background knowledge, connecting the learned inference procedure to the supplied rules. It can also produce symbolic explanations for predictions and can guarantee that logical constraints are satisfied during testing.

The experiments report that A-NeSI is the first end-to-end method to solve three neurosymbolic tasks with exponentially growing combinatorial structure. They also show explainability and constraint-based safety without a performance penalty in those experiments. The contribution is therefore a way to make probabilistic logical reasoning more scalable while preserving useful connections between neural predictions, explicit explanations, and enforceable rules.
neurips-2023-a-nesi-a-scalable-approxima.tldr: A-NeSI uses neural networks to approximate probabilistic logical inference efficiently while supporting symbolic explanations and guaranteed logical constraints.

paragraphs: Transformer attention is usually described through queries, keys, and values. This paper offers another interpretation: attention performs inference over possible connections in a graphical model. Those connections specify which elements relate to one another, so allocating attention becomes a way of reasoning about an implicit structure.

The perspective brings together earlier descriptions involving mixture models, alignment, and Hopfield networks. It also motivates two changes, explored on explanatory toy problems. One expands the value function to include more nodes, creating a tendency to attend to multiple tokens. The other places a geometric prior, with a higher-level prior, over possible connections so that the context window can change with the input.

The authors further discuss a connection to precision regulation in predictive coding networks, suggesting a bridge to Bayesian accounts of attention in neuroscience. The stated contribution is a unifying theoretical viewpoint plus illustrative mechanisms. Its demonstrations show how structural assumptions can shape attention behavior, supporting potential avenues for developing new attention architectures.
neurips-2023-attention-as-implicit-struc.tldr: The paper interprets attention as inference over possible graph connections and uses that view to explore new attention mechanisms.

paragraphs: BeaverTails is a dataset for studying how to align language models with human judgments about safety. Its central design choice is to annotate helpfulness and harmlessness separately for question-answer pairs. This gives researchers distinct information about whether an answer serves the user and whether its content is judged harmless.

The dataset contains safety meta-labels for 333,963 question-answer pairs, along with 361,903 pairs of expert comparison data covering helpfulness and harmlessness. The separate annotation dimensions let researchers examine both attributes explicitly, while the expert comparisons provide preference information about alternative answers. Together, these forms of feedback support studying how human judgments can inform language-model behavior.

The paper demonstrates applications in content moderation and reinforcement learning with human feedback. These examples establish practical uses for the dataset in identifying problematic content and training models from preferences. The contribution is a substantial annotated resource with a clear separation between two alignment objectives, intended to support further research toward safer language-model development and deployment.
neurips-2023-beavertails-towards-improve.tldr: BeaverTails provides human judgments that separate helpfulness from harmlessness to support language-model safety research.

paragraphs: Mind-Video reconstructs videos from continuous fMRI recordings, extending brain-based visual reconstruction beyond static images. The task requires learning information about both visual content and its changes over time. The model progressively learns these spatial and temporal relationships from recordings of the cerebral cortex.

Its training combines masked brain modeling, multimodal contrastive learning with attention across space and time, and joint training with an augmented Stable Diffusion model. That generative model incorporates temporal inflation to support video reconstruction. With adversarial guidance, the authors show that the system can generate high-quality reconstructed videos at arbitrary frame rates.

Evaluation covers both semantic content and pixel-level similarity. The paper reports average semantic classification accuracy of 85%, an SSIM score of 0.19, and a 45% improvement over the previous state of the art. It also presents evidence that the model is interpretable and biologically plausible in ways that reflect established physiological processes. These findings support the approach as a method for recovering continuous visual experiences from brain activity.
neurips-2023-cinematic-mindscapes-high-q.tldr: Mind-Video progressively learns spatial and temporal information from fMRI to reconstruct videos using an augmented diffusion model.

paragraphs: Image-text matching models often train as though every image is correctly paired with its accompanying text. Incorrect pairings violate that assumption and can encourage models to memorize misleading associations. Existing correction methods can also introduce unreliable fixes, especially when the training data contains substantial correspondence noise.

The proposed CRCL framework addresses both problems. Its Active Complementary Loss combines active and complementary learning objectives to reduce the risk of erroneous supervision. Its Self-refining Correspondence Correction repeatedly revises correspondences using momentum correction. This process broadens the information considered during correction and is intended to reduce the accumulation of mistakes across updates.

The paper provides theoretical and experimental support for the loss's robustness to noisy pairings. Experiments on Flickr30K, MS-COCO, and CC152K also show superior robustness for the full framework under synthetic and real-world correspondence noise. The approach matters because it treats noisy supervision and unreliable correction as connected problems: learning should resist incorrect pairs while the correction procedure becomes more accurate and stable.
neurips-2023-cross-modal-active-compleme.tldr: CRCL makes image-text matching more robust by combining a noise-resistant learning objective with iterative correction of mismatched training pairs.

paragraphs: This paper studies how an outside attacker can influence multiple reinforcement-learning agents as they learn. In the considered setting, the attacker can alter rewards before agents receive them or change actions before those actions reach the environment. These access points let the attacker interfere with both feedback and behavior.

The attacker seeks either to steer each agent toward a chosen policy or to increase cumulative rewards according to an attacker-selected objective. At the same time, the attacker wants to minimize the amount of manipulation. The authors first establish limitations of attacks that modify only actions or only rewards, then introduce a strategy that combines the two channels.

They show that the combined strategy can efficiently attack the agents even without prior knowledge of the environment or the agents' learning algorithms. The result identifies a vulnerability within the stated intervention setting: restrictions affecting either channel alone do not prevent an effective mixed attack. This makes the interaction between action manipulation and reward manipulation important for understanding the safety of multi-agent learning.
neurips-2023-efficient-adversarial-attac.tldr: Combining reward and action manipulation enables efficient attacks on multi-agent learners without prior knowledge of their environment or algorithms.

paragraphs: Object recognition systems can perform unevenly across countries and income levels, but aggregate accuracy gaps reveal little about which visual differences accompany those failures. This paper adds detailed factor annotations to Dollar Street, a dataset containing images from economically and geographically diverse settings. The labels describe properties such as color, shape, and background.

These annotations let the researchers compare how objects appear across groups and connect those differences with model vulnerabilities. Across the modern vision models studied, performance disparities are most strongly associated with texture differences, occlusion, and darker lighting. This gives a more specific picture of the conditions associated with recognition failures than group-level performance measurements alone.

The authors also illustrate how these findings can inform mitigation. In one example, addressing a model's sensitivity to texture improves performance for the lower-income group. They release the annotations and an interactive dashboard to support further investigation. The contribution combines a diagnostic resource with evidence that identifying particular visual vulnerabilities can help guide improvements in recognition equity.
neurips-2023-exploring-why-object-recogn.tldr: Detailed image annotations link recognition disparities to visual factors and show how addressing texture sensitivity can improve lower-income performance.

paragraphs: Some black-box optimization problems return a numerical objective value only when an attempted evaluation succeeds. Otherwise, the optimizer learns just that the attempt failed. Several hidden constraints may determine these failures, and even the number of constraints can be unknown. This makes ordinary observations and failure feedback fundamentally different sources of information.

The paper proposes F-GP-UCB, a failure-aware version of Gaussian process upper confidence bound optimization. Its stated assumption about observation failure is that an optimal solution lies inside a feasible region. This condition provides the basis for analyzing progress despite a potentially complicated pattern of unsuccessful evaluations.

The authors prove that successful observations accumulate linearly, then use that result to establish regret upper bounds and convergence for the method. Regret measures the shortfall associated with optimization choices, so these bounds give a formal account of performance over time. Benchmark experiments, including a simulation motivated by material synthesis, demonstrate effectiveness in settings where failed evaluations are part of the optimization problem.
neurips-2023-failure-aware-gaussian-proc.tldr: F-GP-UCB optimizes despite failed evaluations and has convergence and regret guarantees when an optimum lies inside a feasible region.

paragraphs: Local stochastic gradient descent is widely used for distributed and federated training, but its success on nonconvex neural-network objectives is difficult to explain theoretically. This paper analyzes ordinary local SGD for two-layer networks with Gaussian inputs. It establishes global convergence without requiring overparameterization or adding artificial noise.

The proof first identifies a self-correction mechanism. Even when initialization puts the model in a region where gradient descent would move away from the optimum, local SGD can bring both layers into a favorable region in polynomial time. The analysis divides the objective landscape into regions to control how the two layers' dependent gradients interfere with this correction.

Once the model reaches a favorable region, an exact recursive description of the direction of its global parameters establishes convergence to the global minimum. The result also provides linear speedup with the number of machines and reduced communication rounds. Synthetic-data experiments support the theory. The contribution explains how correction and subsequent progress can arise under the paper's specific network and input assumptions.
neurips-2023-global-convergence-analysis.tldr: For two-layer networks with Gaussian inputs, the paper proves local SGD can reach a global minimum without overparameterization or injected noise.

paragraphs: Few-shot learning must generalize from very little labeled target data, making overfitting a central challenge. This paper studies training with additional auxiliary datasets to improve generalization. The difficulty is deciding which auxiliary sources to use: earlier automated mixing approaches become more computationally expensive as the number of candidate datasets grows.

The authors frame that selection problem as a balance between exploration and exploitation. A learner should investigate potentially useful datasets while continuing to use sources that already appear beneficial. They develop EXP3-FLAD and UCB1-FLAD with computational complexity independent of the number of auxiliary datasets, enabling experiments with 100 times as many auxiliary datasets as prior methods.

The experiments find that combining exploration and exploitation is crucial and report a 4% improvement over all pre-existing FLAD methods. They also report 3-billion-parameter language models outperforming the 175-billion-parameter GPT-3 in the evaluated setting. These findings suggest that better data-mixing strategies can substantially improve few-shot generalization and make much larger collections of auxiliary data practical to use.
neurips-2023-improving-few-shot-generali.tldr: Bandit-inspired auxiliary-data selection improves few-shot generalization while scaling to far more candidate datasets than earlier mixing methods.

paragraphs: Feature selection aims to retain useful input properties and make learning more efficient. This paper couples that selection with learning a nearest-neighbor graph. The two decisions are connected: the chosen features affect which samples appear similar, while the graph provides structure for judging which features are informative.

Dirichlet energy links the two parts by measuring how smoothly feature values vary over the graph. The method uses this measure to identify important features and to learn a graph that reflects relationships in the resulting feature subspace. Because constructing a nearest-neighbor graph creates a nondifferentiability problem, the authors use optimal transport theory to make graph learning compatible with neural-network training.

The paper states that this construction is theoretically applicable to dynamic graph learning in other graph neural networks. It also describes the framework as interpretable because its modules are designed algorithmically. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets validate its effectiveness. The central contribution is a coordinated procedure in which feature selection and graph construction can improve together during learning.
neurips-2023-joint-feature-and-different.tldr: The method jointly selects features and learns a differentiable nearest-neighbor graph using Dirichlet energy and optimal transport.

paragraphs: Neural networks learn layered internal representations, but explaining what those representations mean remains difficult. INVERT connects them to human-understandable concepts by examining their ability to distinguish between concepts. The idea is to use a representation's discriminative behavior as evidence for assigning it an explanation.

The method addresses several practical obstacles in earlier global explanation approaches. It supports diverse neuron types, reduces computational complexity, and does not require segmentation masks. It also supplies an interpretable score for how well a representation aligns with its proposed explanation, together with a measure of statistical significance. These outputs make the quality of a concept assignment part of the explanation itself.

The paper demonstrates uses that include locating representations influenced by spurious correlations and interpreting the hierarchical organization of model decisions. These applications show how concept labeling can help investigate both what a model has learned and how that knowledge is organized. The contribution is a scalable explanation method with explicit measures for assessing the correspondence between internal representations and their labels.
neurips-2023-labeling-neural-representat.tldr: INVERT labels neural representations through their ability to distinguish concepts, with alignment scores and statistical significance measures.

paragraphs: Graph neural architecture search automates the design of networks for graph tasks. Extending it to multiple tasks creates another problem: the search must account for how tasks help or influence one another. MTGC3 jointly searches for task-specific architectures and learns collaborative relationships among the tasks.

A layer-wise disentangled supernet manages multiple candidate architectures within one framework. A soft task-collaboration module learns how transferable information is between tasks, allowing those relationships to shape the joint process. The method also uses a task-wise curriculum that adjusts each task's influence according to its difficulty, changing how the search allocates attention across tasks during training.

Across the reported multi-task experiments, MTGC3 achieves state-of-the-art performance against several baselines. The findings support its ability both to discover effective architectures and to capture useful relationships among tasks. The approach matters because architecture choice and inter-task collaboration are learned together, while the curriculum explicitly accounts for differences in difficulty rather than treating every task's contribution as fixed throughout the search.
neurips-2023-multi-task-graph-neural-arc.tldr: MTGC3 jointly searches graph-network architectures and task collaborations while adjusting training influence according to task difficulty.

paragraphs: Genes with similar functions can appear in very different biological datasets, making shared representations difficult to learn. MuSe-GNN addresses this heterogeneity by combining multimodal learning with graph neural networks. It learns from single-cell sequencing and spatial transcriptomic data to place genes in a joint representation space.

The study uses 82 training datasets spanning 10 tissues, three sequencing techniques, and three species. It constructs informative graphs and incorporates weighted similarity learning and contrastive learning as regularization. These components help the model learn gene-to-gene relationships across datasets, so the resulting representations encode functional similarity across different biological contexts.

Benchmarking shows that MuSe-GNN captures gene-function similarity across modalities and reports improvements of up to 100.4% over state-of-the-art gene-representation methods. The authors also combine the representations with bioinformatics tools to investigate pathway enrichment, regulatory causal networks, and disease-associated gene functions. Together, the results support using unified gene representations for analyses that connect gene function with tissues, diseases, and species evolution.
neurips-2023-muse-gnn-learning-unified-g.tldr: MuSe-GNN combines heterogeneous biological graphs to learn shared gene representations that capture functional similarity across contexts.

paragraphs: This paper analyzes linear regression fitted by empirical risk minimization, using a family of losses indexed by p greater than one. It asks how much data is sufficient and how closely the fitted model approaches the best achievable population risk. The results distinguish an exactly representable target from the more general case.

When the target is realizable, the authors show that a sample count proportional to dimension suffices for exact recovery, up to a distribution-dependent constant. This result requires no moment assumptions. In the general case with p at least two, weak moment assumptions on the target and input variables yield a high-probability bound on excess risk.

The leading term of that bound matches the asymptotically exact rate up to a constant depending only on p. The authors extend the result to p between one and two under mild assumptions ensuring that the risk has a Hessian at its minimizer. The contribution gives sharply characterized statistical guarantees while making clear which assumptions support each regime.
neurips-2023-optimal-excess-risk-bounds-.tldr: The paper establishes exact-recovery and sharp excess-risk guarantees for empirical p-norm linear regression under regime-specific assumptions.

paragraphs: Gromov-Wasserstein distance compares distributions whose underlying spaces may differ, making it useful for aligning heterogeneous graph data. However, outliers can strongly distort the comparison when the objective gives them the same weight as ordinary samples. This paper introduces a robust variant, RGW, to reduce that sensitivity.

RGW permits favorable adjustments to the marginal constraints within an ambiguity set defined using Kullback-Leibler divergence. In plain terms, the formulation allows controlled flexibility in how distributional mass participates in the alignment. That flexibility is the mechanism used to address the inaccuracies caused by outliers in the original comparison objective.

The authors also develop a computationally efficient solution procedure based on Bregman proximal alternating linearized minimization and provide theoretical support for it. Experiments validate the theoretical results and demonstrate effectiveness on real-world graph tasks, including subgraph matching and partial shape correspondence. The contribution combines a more robust comparison objective with a practical optimization method, making the proposed treatment of outliers usable in graph alignment problems.
neurips-2023-outlier-robust-gromov-wasse.tldr: RGW makes Gromov-Wasserstein graph alignment more resistant to outliers through controlled flexibility in its marginal constraints.

paragraphs: Human preferences often judge complete generated answers, while a language model trains and generates one token at a time. This mismatch in granularity can complicate learning because an overall preference does not directly specify guidance for individual token decisions. The paper develops a training process that explicitly connects these two levels.

The process alternates between learning token-level guidance from sequence-level preferences and improving the language model using that guidance. Its guidance framework extends pairwise preference learning from imitation learning to variable-length text and preferences involving multiple generations. This lets the method accommodate the structure of language-model outputs and make use of comparisons beyond a single pair.

For updating the language model, the authors present two simple objectives suited to different amounts of supervised data. Experiments on discrete-prompt generation and text summarization show competitive performance. The findings support the usefulness of translating whole-output preferences into finer-grained training guidance, with an alternating procedure that learns the guidance and then applies it to model improvement.
neurips-2023-preference-grounded-token-l.tldr: The method alternates between converting sequence-level preferences into token-level guidance and fine-tuning a language model with that guidance.

paragraphs: Cross-modal retrieval matches visual content with language by learning a shared representation space. Its predictions can become unreliable when the data itself is ambiguous, such as damaged images, rapidly changing videos, or vague descriptions. PAU focuses on quantifying this data-driven, or aleatoric, uncertainty alongside retrieval predictions.

The framework first learns a collection of prototypes for each modality to represent its semantic space. It then uses Dempster-Shafer theory and subjective logic to build an evidence-based uncertainty framework, linking evidence to parameters of a Dirichlet distribution. This connects the model's representation of semantic content with a formal account of uncertainty about its predictions.

Experiments on MSR-VTT, MSVD, DiDeMo, and MS-COCO demonstrate the method's effectiveness. The authors report accurate uncertainty estimates and reliable retrieval predictions. The contribution is a mechanism for making ambiguity in the input data explicit, so a retrieval system can characterize uncertainty as well as produce a match. Its prototype-based construction ties that characterization to learned semantic representations in both vision and language.
neurips-2023-prototype-based-aleatoric-u.tldr: PAU uses learned semantic prototypes and an evidential framework to quantify data ambiguity in vision-language retrieval.

paragraphs: MindEye uses fMRI recordings to retrieve and reconstruct images a person viewed. It maps brain activity into a high-dimensional multimodal representation space, such as CLIP's image space. Generative models that accept those representations can then use the mapped activity to produce an image reconstruction.

The system has two parallel components with distinct specializations: contrastive learning supports retrieval, while a diffusion prior supports reconstruction. This separation addresses the different demands of identifying an existing image and generating a visual reconstruction. A further approach uses outputs from a separate autoencoder with img2img to better preserve low-level image features.

The reported qualitative and quantitative comparisons show state-of-the-art performance on both tasks. MindEye can identify the exact viewed image among highly similar candidates and retrieve accurately from a large database such as LAION-5B, indicating retention of fine-grained image information. Ablation studies attribute improvements to the specialized components, improved training techniques, and much larger models. Together, the findings connect effective brain representations with both precise retrieval and image generation.
neurips-2023-reconstructing-the-mind-s-e.tldr: MindEye maps fMRI activity into image representations using specialized components for precise image retrieval and generative reconstruction.

paragraphs: Multiple instance learning supports weakly supervised tasks such as classifying whole-slide medical images. This paper shows that models performing well within one domain can deteriorate when tested in another, such as a different hospital. RAM-MIL addresses this problem by adding retrieval of related data to the learning framework.

The approach uses optimal transport as the distance measure for nearest-neighbor retrieval. Its motivation connects two ideas: the authors' theoretical finding that lower intrinsic input dimension can reduce approximation error in attention-based MIL, and earlier findings relating intrinsic dimension to merging input features with retrieved data. These ideas motivate using retrieval to improve the representation supplied to the model.

Whole-slide classification experiments report state-of-the-art performance when training and retrieval data share a domain and when unlabeled retrieval data comes from another domain. Optimal transport also supplies a transportation matrix that makes retrieval correspondences interpretable at the instance level. Those correspondences can be visualized for experts, coupling the reported predictive improvements with a way to inspect the retrieved information.
neurips-2023-retrieval-augmented-multipl.tldr: RAM-MIL uses optimal-transport retrieval to improve whole-slide classification across domains and expose interpretable instance-level correspondences.

paragraphs: Acoustic matching changes an audio recording so that it sounds as though it came from a target environment. Earlier methods require paired training recordings that represent both source and target acoustics. Obtaining those pairs can restrict training diversity or require simulated examples and heuristic pairing procedures.

This paper learns from a target scene image and its audio, without needing a corresponding recording with mismatched source acoustics. A conditional generative adversarial framework jointly learns to separate room acoustics from the audio and resynthesize it for the target setting. A new metric measures how much acoustic information remains in the audio after the method tries to remove its existing acoustic influence.

The authors train with either web recordings collected in the wild or simulated data. They report improvements over the state of the art across multiple challenging datasets and varied real-world recordings and environments. The result supports learning acoustic transformation from less restrictive training examples, while jointly addressing removal of existing acoustic characteristics and synthesis of the desired ones.
neurips-2023-self-supervised-visual-acou.tldr: The method learns to match audio to a pictured acoustic environment without paired source-and-target acoustic recordings.

paragraphs: Autonomous learning agents may face social dilemmas in which standard game-theoretic reasoning predicts a failure to cooperate. Earlier work showed that access to one another's source code or model weights can enable cooperation in the one-shot Prisoner's Dilemma. However, full transparency can be unrealistic, and learning cooperative behavior in that setting can be difficult.

This paper studies a more limited information channel: each agent sees a single number describing how similar it is to the other agent. The authors prove that their similarity-based setting permits the same set of cooperative outcomes as the full-transparency setting. Thus, within the proposed framework, the available cooperative outcomes can be preserved despite the much narrower observation.

The paper also demonstrates experimentally that simple machine-learning methods can learn cooperation in this setting. The theoretical result concerns which outcomes are possible, while the experiments address whether learning can reach cooperative behavior. Together, they show how partial information about another agent can provide a basis for cooperation without requiring access to its complete implementation.
neurips-2023-similarity-based-cooperativ.tldr: In the proposed setting, a single similarity signal permits the same cooperative outcomes as full transparency, and simple learning methods can learn cooperation.

paragraphs: Social navigation robots need to detect nearby people, track them, and predict where they will move. SiT is a pedestrian-trajectory dataset designed to support this connected set of tasks. Its recordings were collected while a robot moved through crowded environments, capturing interactions between pedestrians and a moving robot.

The dataset includes sequential measurements from two 3D LiDARs, five cameras providing a full surrounding view, two inertial sensors, and real-time kinematic positioning. Annotations include two-dimensional and three-dimensional boxes, object categories, and identifiers. These complementary data types support following objects over time and relating their trajectories to the robot's changing surroundings.

SiT is organized for training and evaluating a unified pipeline spanning 3D detection, multi-object tracking, and trajectory prediction. The authors provide a benchmark covering these tasks and evaluate multiple baseline models. They also release the dataset, development tools, and pretrained models publicly. The contribution is a shared resource for studying pedestrian prediction in moving human-robot interactions, with potential to support safer and more agile navigation.
neurips-2023-sit-dataset-socially-intera.tldr: SiT provides sensor recordings and annotations from a moving robot to benchmark pedestrian detection, tracking, and trajectory prediction.

paragraphs: Length generalization asks whether a model trained on shorter sequences can handle longer ones. This paper systematically compares five positional approaches in decoder-only Transformers: absolute embeddings, T5 relative encoding, ALiBi, rotary encoding, and no explicit positional encoding. The evaluation uses a collection of reasoning and mathematical tasks.

In those experiments, common choices including absolute embeddings, ALiBi, and rotary encoding perform poorly at length generalization. Models without explicit positional encoding outperform the explicit alternatives while requiring no additional computation. The authors also prove that such models can represent both absolute and relative positional encodings, showing that omitting an explicit encoding does not eliminate that representational capability.

When trained with stochastic gradient descent, the models without positional encoding mostly develop attention patterns resembling T5's relative encoding. The study further finds that scratchpads do not always help, and their format strongly affects performance. Together, the results suggest that explicit positional embeddings are not essential for good length generalization in decoder-only Transformers, while highlighting the importance of task and representation choices.
neurips-2023-the-impact-of-positional-en.tldr: Across tested reasoning and math tasks, decoder-only Transformers without explicit positional encoding generalize to longer sequences better than the compared alternatives.

paragraphs: This paper studies how Transformer weights change during learning. Its central observation concerns the difference between the current weights and their initial values: that difference progressively increases in rank. Rank describes the number of independent directions represented by a matrix, so the finding characterizes an incremental expansion in the structure of learned changes.

The authors rigorously prove this behavior under two simplifying assumptions: the weight matrices are diagonal, and initialization is small. Under those conditions, gradual rank growth is a mathematical property of the analyzed learning dynamics. The result gives a precise description of how parameter changes develop during training, with the assumptions defining the scope of the proof.

Experiments support the theoretical analysis and also show that the phenomenon can occur without those simplifying assumptions. This extends the evidence beyond the exact setting covered by the proof, while retaining an empirical claim about the broader case. The contribution is an account of incremental learning based on the evolving rank of weight updates relative to initialization.
neurips-2023-transformers-learn-through-.tldr: Transformer weight changes can grow gradually in rank, with a proof under simplifying assumptions and supporting experiments beyond them.
